record.paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
record.context_brief: Embedding linear functional equations into flows
record.original_question: Given functions f, g, and h in the linear functional equation φ(f(x)) = g(x)φ(x) + h(x), under what weak assumptions on f, g, and h can this discrete-time equation be embedded into a continuous-time family φ(F(t,x)) = G(t,x)φ(x) + H(t,x), where F, G, and H satisfy the natural flow and cocycle identities and interpolate the original data at t = 1?

evidence.quote: The following problem concerning the linear equation ϕ(f(x)) = g(x)ϕ(x) + h(x) (10.5) was posed by L. Reich [213]. He asked under what possibly weak assumptions on the given functions f, g, h we can "embed" (10.5) in the equation with "continuous time" argument: ϕ(F(t, x)) = G(t, x)ϕ(x) + H(t, x). (10.6)

More precisely: under what assumptions on f, g, h there exist F, G, H from a suitable class of functions solving equations F(t + s, x) = F(t, F(s, x)), G(t + s, x) = G(s, x)G(t, F(s, x)), H(t + s, x) = G(t, F(s, x))H(s, x) + H(t, F(s, x)) and fulfilling conditions F(1, ·) = f, G(0, ·)=1, G(1, ·) = g, H(0, ·)=0, H(1, ·) = h such that every solution of (10.5) from the considered function class satisfies equation (10.6).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a nonempty set (e.g. an interval of the real line or an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$) and consider the linear functional equation in a single unknown function $\varphi : X \to \mathbb{R}$:
$$\varphi(f(x)) = g(x)\,\varphi(x) + h(x), \qquad x \in X, \tag{1}$$
where $f : X \to X$, $g : X \to \mathbb{R}$ and $h : X \to \mathbb{R}$ are given.

Say that equation (1) can be embedded in a continuous-time family if there exist functions
$$F : T \times X \to X, \quad G : T \times X \to \mathbb{R}, \quad H : T \times X \to \mathbb{R},$$
defined on $T \times X$ where $T$ is an interval containing $\{0,1\}$ (e.g. $T=[0,\infty)$ or $T=\mathbb{R}$), satisfying the cocycle/flow identities
$$F(t+s, x) = F(t, F(s, x)),$$
$$G(t+s, x) = G(s, x)\,G(t, F(s, x)),$$
$$H(t+s, x) = G(t, F(s, x))\,H(s, x) + H(t, F(s, x)),$$
together with the interpolation conditions
$$F(1, \cdot) = f, \quad G(0, \cdot) = 1, \quad G(1, \cdot) = g, \quad H(0, \cdot) = 0, \quad H(1, \cdot) = h,$$
such that every solution $\varphi$ of (1), within a prescribed regularity class, also satisfies the continuous-time equation
$$\varphi(F(t, x)) = G(t, x)\,\varphi(x) + H(t, x), \qquad (t,x) \in T \times X. \tag{2}$$

Problem. Determine the weakest possible regularity/structural assumptions on $f$, $g$, $h$ (and on the considered class of solutions $\varphi$) under which such an embedding into a continuous-time family $(F, G, H)$ exists; equivalently, characterize those triples $(f, g, h)$ for which (1) embeds into (2) in the above sense.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return decisive evidence on the current status of L. Reich's embedding problem for the linear functional equation φ(f(x)) = g(x)φ(x) + h(x) into a continuous-time cocycle family. While embedding problems for the homogeneous case (h ≡ 0) and for iteration of f are classically studied, no source confirming a complete solution of the inhomogeneous embedding problem under weak assumptions was located.
